items.stem: You need the actual exception message text for a failing run. Which diagnostic script is the right starting point?
items.explanation: ExceptionRejections joins Operation -> Message to surface the rejection/warning/exception text.

misconceptions.d: Cleanup mutates data — never reach for it just to read messages.

items.stem: A user reports a record showing up twice in the destination. Which script finds the cause?

options.text: Starbridge-SeeMappingIssues.sql (records with more than one active mapping)

items.explanation: SeeMappingIssues groups mappings and flags those with COUNT(*) > 1 — duplicate active mappings are the usual cause of a doubled record.

misconceptions.b: ValueChange shows field diffs, not duplicate mappings.

items.stem: In Starbridge-ExceptionRejections.sql, a Message Type of 3 means:
items.explanation: Type codes: 1 = Rejection, 2 = Warning, 3 = Exception, 4 = Information.

misconceptions.a: Rejection is Type 1; exceptions are Type 3.

items.stem: A teammate is about to run Starbridge-Cleanup.sql on production just to 'see what's failing'. What do you advise?
rubric: Cleanup-type scripts mutate data — they are not for read-only diagnosis
For 'what's failing' use a read-only script (ExceptionRejections / Transactions) instead
Read any script before running it; prefer read-only scripts on production
items.sampleAnswer: Don't — Cleanup mutates StarBridge data and isn't a diagnostic. To see what's failing, run a read-only script like ExceptionRejections (for the message text) or Transactions (for outcomes). Always read a script before running it, especially on production.
items.source: DiagnosticScripts/When and How to use these scripts.docx

items.stem: Where does the exception text live (not just the outcome), and how does ExceptionRejections.sql get it?
rubric: The text is in the Message table, linked to an Operation via OperationMessage
ExceptionRejections joins Operation -> OperationMessage -> Message (and out to EntityType / SourceSystemEntityId) and filters by Message Type
items.sampleAnswer: The message text is in the Message table, tied to an Operation through OperationMessage. ExceptionRejections does those joins (Operation -> OperationMessage -> Message, plus EntityType/SourceSystemEntityId) so you can read the exception/rejection text by Type.
